contracts.name: adoption

R16.4 a failing runner command shows the last lines of its standard error, and a missing module or program is reported as contracts that cannot run here, by check and by audit, with a non-zero exit
R16.5 a runner testcase name with the criterion ID in underscores or in a parametrize id maps to that criterion as "R1.1 ...", and the gate requires it by criterion
R16.6 necro help, --help and -h print each command with one line on what it does, and init from an npx cache warns and shows how to install permanently

contracts.name: audit-fast
names: R14.7 stop and posttask run only the contracts of the task ticked since the freeze and untick it; the others are left alone
R14.7 posttask runs no contract when no task was ticked since the freeze
R14.7 necro audit still checks every ticked task, and changes nothing
R14.8 the README says receipts are files an agent can add, and what a forged receipt can and cannot do
R14.9 CI runs necro audit and re-runs the newest receipt of each spec of the two examples only

contracts.name: audit-upgrade

contracts.name: audit

R14.2 necro audit changes no file
R14.3 necro hook stop and necro hook posttask, given any or empty input, untick every task that is not ok, say why on stderr and leave ok tasks alone
R14.4 necro init writes a PostTaskExec hook that runs necro hook posttask in the hooks file and the custom agent, with the same timeout as the others

R3.2 a write tool call to any path under .necro/ exits 2

R3.11 a non-read-only tool call with a too long or NUL-containing input string is blocked

R13.17 source code that sets assert.ok, assert.equal and assert.strictEqual to a no-op makes its contract fail, not pass (a plain assignment)
R13.17 source code that sets assert.ok, assert.equal and assert.strictEqual to a no-op makes its contract fail, not pass (Object.defineProperty)
R13.17 source code that sets assert.ok, assert.equal and assert.strictEqual to a no-op makes its contract fail, not pass (Object.assign on the module a require returns)
R13.17 source code that sets assert.ok, assert.equal and assert.strictEqual to a no-op makes its contract fail, not pass (a CommonJS file in sloppy mode, where the write fails without an error)
R13.17 source code that replaces a function of node:test makes its contract fail, not pass

R13.18 plain() returns a new built-in Error with the message and name of the one given, never that object
R13.18 plain() returns a new built-in RegExp with the source and flags of the one given, never that object
R13.18 a contract that asks a lying RegExp or Error to describe itself passes; one that compares plain(result) fails

contracts.name: cheats
names: R13.15 a contract file runs in a process started with --frozen-intrinsics, so the built-in prototypes cannot be changed

R13.15 necro check and its receipt agree: the prototype patch is not a pass, the honest report is
R13.16 plain() returns primitive strings, plain arrays, plain objects and Map copies, and ignores every method a subclass doctors
R13.16 a contract that compares plain(result) is not fooled by the String subclass that passed an impossible contract
R13.16 the README tells contract authors to compare plain values
R15.9 a function that changes its own argument cannot make its check agree with a wrong result
R15.9 the check gets a deep copy: nested values, Maps, Sets and Dates are copied, and a check that changes its copy changes nothing else
R15.9 a value that cannot be cloned falls back to the original, and the other arguments are still copied

R15.10 the example guards parseLedger in bin/ledger.js, with a table in postconditions.js that recomputes each line from the text

contracts.name: gate

R4.13 a write to a tasks.md that leaves more [x] task lines than the file on disk is gated, even when no line matches an earlier [ ] line
R4.19 task_update with status completed is gated like a tick written to tasks.md, with the same exit codes, messages and receipt
R4.20 a task_update to completed that names no task line requires every contract; a path outside the project is blocked

contracts.name: init
names: R8.1 init writes .kiro/hooks/necromancer.json with PreToolUse, PostToolUse and Stop hooks that call necro hook pre, post and stop, each with a timeout of 300 seconds

contracts.name: lock-restore

contracts.name: lock
names: R2.1 freeze records the SHA-256 of requirements.md and of every contract file in .necro/lock.json
R2.2 freeze stores a copy of each frozen file at .necro/frozen/<sha256>
R2.3 freeze refuses when contracts/<spec>/ has no contract files and says at least one is needed
R2.4 freezing again replaces that spec's entry and keeps other specs' entries unchanged
R2.5 freeze runs the contracts once and records the name of every contract in the lock
R2.6 freeze refuses a contract whose path resolves outside the project root
R2.7 freeze records, for each task in tasks.md, the task id and the criteria its line names
R2.8 freeze records each task's full line text after the checkbox

contracts.name: mcp
names: R10.1 necro mcp answers initialize, ignores notifications, answers ping and tools/list, and exits 0 when stdin closes, writing only JSON-RPC messages to stdout and using no dependencies
R10.2 tools/list offers exactly necro_status, necro_check and necro_verify with input schemas, and each tool returns what Requirement 10 says
R10.3 no tool freezes, edits or ticks, and an unknown tool, an unfrozen spec and malformed JSON each get an error reply while the server keeps running

contracts.name: person-freeze

R8.8 init writes a steering file saying a person freezes specs, the agent never runs necro freeze, and frozen specs are listed in .necro/lock.json

contracts.name: python-example

contracts.name: receipts
names: R5.1 a receipt records the spec, the git commit if available, and the hashes of the requirements, the contracts and the imported sources, with each result by name
R5.2 receiptHash is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the receipt without receiptHash and createdAt
R5.3 receipts made from identical inputs have the same receiptHash
R5.4 in a git repository a receipt records in uncommitted the sorted pinned paths that differ from the recorded commit, or [] when none do
R5.5 a receipt records task (the ticked task id and its line) and required (the sorted required contract names), and still every result

contracts.name: required
names: R4.14 a tick requires the contracts whose names start with a criterion the lock records for that task id
R4.15 every contract is required when the ticked task cannot be tied to the criteria the lock recorded
R4.16 every contract is required when the ticked line, the id or the unticked tasks cannot be trusted
R4.17 a contract file that holds a required contract and fails as a whole fails the tick
R4.18 only an unticked line on exactly one line with the frozen text counts as a frozen task that is still unticked

contracts.name: runner-hardening
names: R13.7 a runner command that exits with a non-zero status fails the file even when its report says every testcase passed
R13.7 a non-zero exit with no readable report is one failing contract named after the file, with the status named
R13.7 a runner command that runs past the time limit fails the file with the timeout named, is killed with its children, and leaves no temporary folder
R13.7 the runner time limit is 240 seconds by default, below the hooks limit of 300, and the same limit applies to JavaScript contract files
R13.8 {file} and {report} are replaced in one pass, so a project path that holds {report} or {file} stays intact
R13.8 a runner command gets a fresh empty PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX folder each run, and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
R13.9 the globs under "sources" are pinned in the receipt, and necro verify prints MISMATCH when one of the files changes
R13.9 the files under "frozen" are locked with the spec: the gate refuses edits and puts them back, check fails while one differs, receipts pin them
R13.9 a spec whose runners.json has neither key gets a lock and receipts without "frozen" and with no sources
R13.9 a glob under "frozen" or "sources" that matches no file refuses the freeze with a plain sentence
R13.10 the README says plainly what runner contracts cannot defend against

contracts.name: runner
names: R4.7 a contract reported as skipped or todo counts as failing
R4.8 a frozen spec whose contract files contain zero contracts is refused, not passed
R4.9 a contract file whose hash differs from the lock when it is run makes every contract in that file fail
R4.10 a contract name recorded in the lock that is missing from a run counts as failing
R4.11 contract names are kept exactly as reported, and only the file's own path is a file load failure
R4.12 results come from the Node test runner's events, never from text the code under test prints, and names are matched per file

contracts.name: runners
names: R13.1 files matching a pattern in runners.json are contract files of the spec in freeze, check, the gate and verify
R13.2 a contract file runs its command without a shell, with {file} and a new {report} path, and results come only from the report
R13.3 testcase names are contract names, and the gate requires the contracts of the ticked task by criterion
R13.4 a missing command, no report, bad XML and an empty report each fail the file, with the file named

R15.6 the README explains runtime postconditions as Eiffel's ensure, their cost, and what they catch that tests cannot

contracts.name: shell
names: R3.3 after a shell command, a frozen file whose SHA-256 changed is restored and named on stderr

contracts.name: verify-root

contracts.name: verify
names: R6.1 verify prints CONFIRMED and the receipt hash and exits 0 when every hashed file matches and the contracts give the same results
R6.2 verify prints MISMATCH with each differing path and exits 1 when a hashed file differs
R6.3 verify prints MISMATCH with each differing contract name and exits 1 when a contract result differs
